title: Elastic bar striking a rigid wall (explicit)
source: One-dimensional elastic impact on a rigid wall: contact time 2L/c, rebound at the impact speed, contact stress ρcv₀; Graff, Wave Motion in Elastic Solids, Dover 1991, §2.3; Johnson, Impact Strength of Materials, Arnold 1972, §1.6

quantities.quantity: displacement of the struck end at t = 0.3 (in contact until 2L/c = 0.2, then leaving at v₀)
quantities.reason: the contact ends at 2L/c in the elastic theory; the discrete release front is spread over a few elements, a few tenths of a percent of the time, and the rebound speed is v₀ to about 1%

quantities.quantity: displacement of the far end at t = 0.3 (−v₀L/c, then +v₀ after the reflection)
kinetic energy after the rebound over the initial ½mv₀²
quantities.reason: an elastic impact keeps the kinetic energy; quadratic bulk viscosity in the compression front and the vibration left in the bar take about 1%
